**Finding submitted: MISSING (critical)**

The Site Development and Hosting Agreement has **no indemnification provision at all** — searches for "indemnif" and "hold harmless" returned zero hits, and the document runs directly from Section 9 (Warranties) to Section 10 (General Provisions).

This is a significant exposure for us: HDI designs, develops, hosts, operates and maintains the Site on its own server, using its own software and Content administration tools (§§ 1.1–1.4), yet bears no obligation to defend us against third-party IP infringement claims arising from those deliverables, its breaches of law, data incidents, or its own gross negligence/wilful misconduct.

**Redline inserted** (validated `ok:true`) as new Section 9A after the Warranties section:
- **9A.1** — HDI defends/indemnifies us and our affiliates for third-party IP claims relating to the Site and HDI's services/software/tools, HDI's breach of law, unauthorised access to Confidential Information/Content/user data caused by HDI, and HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
- **9A.2** — Our reciprocal indemnity kept deliberately narrow: only the Content and Marks we supply, plus our own breach of law.
- **9A.3** — Standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, with consent required for settlements binding the indemnified party, plus an express survival statement (existing § 10.7 survival lists Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 and would not otherwise capture the new section).

Numbering used "9A" to avoid cascading renumbering of Section 10's eight subsections and the § 10.7 survival cross-reference. If HDI pushes back, the sensible fallback is customary IP exclusions (our modifications, combinations, specifications) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies — not deletion of the indemnity.
